---
title: "Self-Attention"
description: "An attention operation in which elements of a sequence use one another to form context-aware representations."
term: "Self-Attention"
letter: "S"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Self-attention lets each token in a sequence look at other tokens in that
same sequence and combine useful information from them. This helps a word's
representation depend on its surrounding context.

## Technical explanation

Self-attention projects an input sequence into queries, keys, and values.
Scaled dot-product attention computes
$\mathrm{softmax}(QK^\mathsf{T}/\sqrt{d_k})V$. Masks can restrict which
positions are visible; causal self-attention prevents a language model from
attending to future tokens.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Self-attention is a core component of Transformer models for language,
vision, and other modalities. Its pairwise interactions can be expensive
for long sequences, motivating efficient attention methods and careful
context-length choices.

## How it works

For each token, the query is compared with keys from allowed positions.
Softmax converts scores into weights, which combine the corresponding
values. Multiple heads can perform separate learned attention operations
and combine their outputs.

The sketch focuses on one token's attention; a full layer computes
attention for all positions and may use multiple heads.

## Practical example

In the sentence “The animal did not cross the road because it was tired,”
self-attention can help the representation of “it” incorporate information
from “animal.” Attention weights are part of the computation, not a complete
explanation of the model's reasoning.

## Common misconceptions

- Self-attention operates within the same input sequence; cross-attention
  attends to a separate sequence.
- Standard full self-attention does not inherently know token order;
  positional information is supplied separately or through the attention
  mechanism.
